questions.stem: Which AWS service is the primary destination for metrics, logs, and alarms?
questions.explanation: CloudWatch is the unified metrics+logs+alarms service. CloudTrail records API calls; X-Ray handles traces.

questions.stem: Memory utilisation on an EC2 instance is NOT visible to CloudWatch by default because:
choices: The hypervisor cannot read guest OS memory; you need the CloudWatch Agent
Memory is on the instance store
questions.explanation: The hypervisor sees CPU and network but not in-guest metrics. The CloudWatch Agent (or third-party) reads them from the OS.

questions.stem: An alarm transitions to ALARM state when:
choices: The metric breaches threshold for the configured number of evaluation periods
Any single data point crosses the threshold
questions.explanation: An alarm fires after the threshold is breached for the configured consecutive evaluation periods, not on a single data point.

questions.stem: Which is NOT one of the four Google SRE 'golden signals'?
questions.explanation: The four golden signals are Latency, Traffic, Errors, and Saturation. Bandwidth is a component of saturation.

questions.stem: Which AWS service provides distributed tracing for microservices?
questions.explanation: X-Ray captures end-to-end traces across services, producing a service map of latencies and errors.

questions.stem: EventBridge is the rebranded successor of which legacy service?
questions.explanation: EventBridge supersedes CloudWatch Events, adding custom buses, schema registry, and partner sources.

questions.stem: An EventBridge rule selects events using:
questions.explanation: Rules match events against JSON patterns; matching events are delivered to configured targets.

questions.stem: Which AWS service records every API call made in the account for audit?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail is the auditable record of management and (optionally) data events for every AWS API call.

questions.stem: CloudWatch Logs Insights is best described as:
choices: An interactive query language over log groups
questions.explanation: Logs Insights provides an interactive query language for searching and aggregating CloudWatch Logs.

questions.stem: A CloudWatch alarm action can trigger:
choices: SNS, Auto Scaling policy, EC2 action, Systems Manager Incident Manager
questions.explanation: Alarm actions can publish to SNS, invoke ASG scaling policies, perform EC2 actions (stop/terminate/reboot), or trigger Incident Manager.

questions.stem: An anomaly-detection alarm:
choices: Builds an ML model of expected values and alarms on deviations
Is the same as a composite alarm
questions.explanation: Anomaly detection learns expected behaviour and alarms when actual values deviate from the model's confidence band.

questions.stem: Which log format makes it easier to search and aggregate later?
questions.explanation: Structured JSON logs are parseable by Logs Insights, EMF-extractable to metrics, and consistent for downstream tools.

questions.stem: EMF (Embedded Metric Format) lets you:
choices: Emit metrics by logging a specific JSON shape
questions.explanation: EMF logs include metric directives; CloudWatch auto-extracts metrics without separate PutMetricData API calls.

questions.stem: Which CloudWatch metric resolution incurs additional cost?
questions.explanation: High-resolution metrics (1-second granularity) cost more than standard 1-minute metrics.

questions.stem: A composite alarm:
choices: Combines other alarms with AND/OR to reduce noise
Is the only alarm type for Lambda
questions.explanation: Composite alarms apply boolean logic across child alarms — e.g. alarm only when CPU high AND latency high AND not in maintenance.

questions.stem: Lambda function metrics include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Lambda doesn't expose an InstanceId metric; the standard Lambda metrics are Invocations, Duration, Errors, Throttles, ConcurrentExecutions.

questions.stem: X-Ray sampling default is approximately:
questions.explanation: Default sampling captures 1 request/sec per host plus 5% of additional requests; sampling rules are configurable.

questions.stem: Which service replaced CloudWatch cron rules with a higher-quota dedicated service?
questions.explanation: EventBridge Scheduler is the dedicated scheduling service with higher quotas and richer features than CloudWatch Events cron rules.

questions.stem: Which is the best mechanism for forwarding CloudWatch Logs in near-real-time to an external SIEM?
choices: Subscription filter to Kinesis Data Firehose
questions.explanation: Subscription filters stream matching logs to Firehose/Kinesis/Lambda for real-time downstream processing.

questions.stem: VPC Flow Logs capture:
choices: Metadata about IP traffic going to/from ENIs (no payload)
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs record flow metadata (src/dst, ports, bytes, accept/reject) but not the packet contents.

questions.stem: Which AWS service is the open-standard tracing/metrics SDK companion to X-Ray?
questions.explanation: ADOT is AWS's distribution of OpenTelemetry with exporters for CloudWatch and X-Ray.

questions.stem: An alarm with TreatMissingData = 'breaching' will:
choices: Transition to ALARM when no data points arrive
questions.explanation: TreatMissingData controls how missing samples are treated; 'breaching' counts them as failures and will move the alarm to ALARM.

questions.stem: RUM (Real User Monitoring) on CloudWatch is used for:
choices: Capturing browser-side performance and errors from real end-user sessions
questions.explanation: CloudWatch RUM collects browser performance and JS errors from real users to track client-side experience.

questions.stem: Synthetic monitoring in CloudWatch is provided by:
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Synthetics Canaries run scheduled scripts that probe endpoints, providing uptime and functional monitoring.

questions.stem: If a Lambda function logs to stdout, the logs:
choices: Are automatically sent to a CloudWatch Log Group for the function
questions.explanation: The Lambda execution environment ships stdout/stderr automatically to a per-function CloudWatch Log Group.
